blocks.text: Quick verdict

SOAX is the better choice for rotating residential and mobile traffic at scale, ad verification and multi-country campaigns, thanks to its large network, ISP-level targeting and unusual protocol support. Proxys.io is the better choice for fixed identities on long-lived accounts and for heavy-bandwidth mobile use, where its flat-rate mobile proxies avoid per-GB charges entirely, and its 24-hour refund window lowers risk. Remember that SOAX credits expire 60 days after purchase.

Proxys.io and SOAX both sell mobile and residential proxies to social media and marketing teams, but through different models. Proxys.io rents fixed IPs and SIM-based mobile proxies with a minimum one-month static rental, often with unlimited bandwidth. SOAX sells access to 155M residential and 33M mobile IPs on one credit balance, with ISP targeting, UDP and QUIC support and per-GB rates set by country tier. This comparison helps you pick the right model for account work and data collection.

blocks.text: Proxys.io in 2026: what you get

PROXYS.IO offers both rented static addresses and a rotating residential network. The provider reports more than 100 million ISP addresses across 195 countries, country/region/city targeting, up to 100 saved parameter sets and rotation every 2-60 minutes. Its mobile service covers 14 countries with city/carrier selection and roughly 2,000-5,000 addresses per country/carrier combination. Static IPv4 covers 24 markets. These are supplied specifications, not independently measured availability. HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 are included on every plan.

Strengths: Low-entry per-address products; a provider-reported 100M+ residential network; country, region and city targeting; HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 included; a 24-hour refund window. Weak spots: Rotating mobile traffic pricing must be checked in the cart; residential plans have 30/60/90-day validity; published pool totals do not guarantee reachable IPs; independent target-specific performance has not been established here.
SOAX in 2026: what you get

SOAX is a residential and mobile specialist known for granular filtering. Its 2026 pricing replaced fixed GB bundles with plans (Sandbox, Builder, Team, Scale, Enterprise) that include credits, and the credit burn rate depends on the exit country's tier. That makes SOAX cheap for some geographies and expensive for low-volume US work. The network is large (155M residential, 33M mobile advertised) and supports protocols few competitors offer, including UDP and QUIC.

Strengths: Residential and mobile on one balance; UDP and QUIC support alongside SOCKS5; Large pool with city and ISP targeting on every plan; Cheap traffic for Tier 2 and Tier 3 countries. Weak spots: Credits expire after 60 days; US traffic is expensive on small plans; Datacenter and ISP proxies were discontinued.
Pricing: Proxys.io vs SOAX

PROXYS.IO separates traffic-based plans from per-address rentals. Rotating residential starts at $1.50/GB on 30, 60 or 90-day plans, without an IP or session cap. Static monthly starting prices are IPv6 $0.13, dynamic $0.27, shared IPv4 $0.67 (up to three users), foreign individual IPv4 $1.47, Windows-fingerprint IPv4 $1.87 and premium static residential IPv4 $3.60. Dedicated mobile IPv4 with unlimited traffic on a private channel starts at $56.79/month. Rotating mobile traffic is priced by the cart slider; no single starting per-GB rate has been confirmed. HEAT_RES provides 35% off eligible residential pay-per-traffic plans. Minimum static rental is one month and the refund window is 24 hours.

SOAX bills prepaid credits. For US (Tier 1) traffic, the no-fee Sandbox plan costs $5/GB, Builder ($200/month) $3/GB, Team ($500/month) $2.20/GB, and Scale ($1,500/month) $1.50/GB; cheaper countries cost less (Tier 3 from $2/GB on Sandbox). Credits expire 60 days after purchase, and SOAX counts traffic in both directions.

At 10 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; SOAX comes to about $50. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; SOAX comes to about $300. Both Proxys.io and SOAX work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

PROXYS.IO reports a residential pool of 100M+ ISP addresses; this has not been independently audited. Proxys.io reports 100M+ addresses and SOAX lists '155M residential + 33M mobile'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Proxys.io lists 195 residential countries, with separate mobile and static coverage countries and SOAX lists 195. On targeting, Proxys.io offers country, region and city for residential traffic, with city/carrier selection for mobile, while SOAX offers country, region, city and ISP; ASN and ZIP on Scale plans.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Proxys.io offers static per-IP proxies; rotating residential and mobile, and SOAX offers rotating or sticky; mobile sessions up to 60 minutes. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: compare the exact target and traffic plan before choosing. PROXYS.IO reports a 100M+ rotating residential network across 195 countries, in addition to static rentals. Pool size alone does not establish success rate; this brief does not independently benchmark PROXYS.IO against the other provider.
SERP and rank tracking: SOAX wins. The deciding factor for SOAX: city and ISP targeting for local results. The limitation on the Proxys.io side: cheap IPv6 can handle some search tasks.

Social media and multi-account management: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Proxys.io: fixed dedicated or mobile IPs per account. SOAX: mobile IPs on the same balance as residential. Let price and the countries you need decide.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: SOAX. SOAX has the edge here. Why: granular location filters. How Proxys.io compares: limited rotation for large catalog crawls.
Ad verification and geo-testing: SOAX wins. The deciding factor for SOAX: ISP, ASN and carrier-level targeting. The limitation on the Proxys.io side: limited geo depth.

Tight budgets: Proxys.io wins. The deciding factor for Proxys.io: cheap per-IP rentals with unlimited bandwidth. The limitation on the SOAX side: cheap in Tier 3 countries but pricey for small US jobs.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial. SOAX: Paid 3-day trial, 400 MB for $1.99. Verification and payment rules differ too. Proxys.io: Light; crypto accepted. SOAX: Verification for postpaid and enterprise terms. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Proxys.io and SOAX before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Proxys.io and SOAX is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial; SOAX: paid 3-day trial, 400 MB for $1.99).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Proxys.io comes out ahead in 1, SOAX in 4, and 1 is a tie. That makes SOAX the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Proxys.io is strongest for multi-account and affiliate work that needs fixed IPs, while SOAX is strongest for mobile-first work such as app testing and social platforms. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
